_comment: Field description for the Peregrine solver.
Obstacles are the REAL physical obstacles -- do NOT inflate them by the
robot's size. Give the robot's own footprint under 'robot' instead and
the solver works out the swept shape for every heading itself.
That has to be done per heading, because the configuration-space
obstacle of a polygonal robot is not a polyhedron in (x, y, heading):
its faces satisfy  n_x*x + n_y*y + A*cos(h) + B*sin(h) = c,  which is
planar only for a point robot. Each fixed-heading slice IS exactly a
polygon, so the solver rasterises one slice per heading bin.
The robot polygon is in the ROBOT BODY frame, with the origin at the
odometry tracking point -- the same point whose x/y the value tables
are indexed by. If your tracking point is not the centre of the
chassis, the polygon must be off-centre to match.
Polygons may be concave. Vertex order does not matter. Units are cm,
matching the calibration regression. Omit 'robot' entirely to treat the

robot._comment: A 36 x 36 cm chassis centred on the tracking point.
